title: The Default Effect

scenes.vo: One tiny checkbox changed the decisions of millions of people.

scenes.text: Austria and Germany: next door, very *similar*
scenes.vo: Austria and Germany are neighbours. Similar people, similar way of life.
But in Germany, only about 12 percent of people signed up to donate organs. In Austria, almost everyone.

scenes.text:
Germany: tick the box to say *yes*
Austria: tick the box to say *no*
scenes.vo: The difference? In Germany, you had to tick a box to say yes. In Austria, you were a yes already, and had to tick a box to say no.
And most people never tick the box. So whatever was already chosen for them, won.
This is called the default effect. A default is what's already chosen for you, if you do nothing.

scenes.text:
Notifications: ON
Autoplay: ON
Auto-renew: ON
scenes.vo: Apps know this. That's why notifications, autoplay and auto-renew are switched on from the start.

scenes.text: Check your settings. Make the *good choice* the default.
scenes.vo: So check your settings, and make the good choice the default. Like turning autoplay off.

scenes.text:
Follow *@inquisitive_bytes*
to understand your brain better
scenes.vo: Follow Inquisitive Bytes to understand your brain, one byte at a time.

caption:
Most of us never change what's already chosen for us. ☑️ It's called the default effect, and apps use it every day.

Go check your autoplay setting right now 👀👇
source: Johnson, E. J. & Goldstein, D. (2003). Do Defaults Save Lives? Science, 302(5649).
